name: Dapagliflozin and metformin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Once daily in the morning with food; dapagliflozin 5 to 10 mg with metformin up to 2,000 mg/day

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Drugs that reduce metformin clearance (ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine)

key_interactions.action: Consider lower insulin or sulfonylurea dose.

key_interactions.effect: Contrast kidney injury can precipitate lactic acidosis (label).
key_interactions.action: Hold per label 2.5; recheck eGFR at 48 hours.

serious: Volume depletion and acute kidney injury
Necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's gangrene)

contraindications: eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or end-stage kidney disease
Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis
Serious hypersensitivity to dapagliflozin or metformin
monitoring: Hold for contrast and 3 days before surgery

pk.half_life: Dapagliflozin about 12.9 hours; metformin about 6 hours (plasma)
pk.metabolism: Dapagliflozin: UGT1A9 to inactive glucuronide; metformin: not metabolized
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Dapagliflozin 75% of radioactivity in urine (under 2% unchanged); metformin about 90% unchanged in urine
